```{r, include=F}
library(foreign)
library(tidyverse)
articles <- read.dta("http://www.stata-press.com/data/lf2/couart2.dta")

m_art <- glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, 
             family = poisson, data = articles)
#summary(m_art)
```

## Activity

Use the provided packet to answer the following questions:

* Does the Poisson regression model appear to be a good fit?
* If not, which piece of the model do you think is mis-specified?

\vspace{4cm}

## Rootograms: an overall assessment of model fit

```{r, fig.width=4, fig.height=3}
topmodels::rootogram(m_art)
```

## Rootograms: an overall assessment of model fit

* horizontal axis: possible values for the response variable
* vertical axis (square root scale): predicted count for the model (points) and *observed* counts from the data (bars)
* Assessing whether predicted counts match observed counts
* Lack of fit could be due to:
    * Wrong choice of distribution
    * Additional explanatory variables need to be added to model
    * Issues with shape assumption
    
\vspace{2cm}

## (Randomized) quantile residual plots

```{r echo=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=2.5, message=F, warning=F}
articles |>
  mutate(res = statmod::qresid(m_art)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = phd, y = res)) +
  geom_point(size=0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Prestige of PhD program",
       y = "Quantile residuals")
```

\vspace{1cm}

## Plot lineup

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.height=3.5, fig.width=4}
library(regressinator)

set.seed(70)
qresid_fn <- function(f){
  data.frame(resid = statmod::qresid(f),
             x = model.frame(f)$ment)
}

model_lineup(m_art, fn = qresid_fn, nsim = 20) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = resid)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth() +
  facet_wrap(vars(.sample)) +
  labs(x = "Mentor articles", y = "Quantile residuals") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
  strip.background = element_blank(),
  strip.text.x = element_blank()
)
```

## Quantile residual plot

Plot without the two rows with the most number of mentor publications:

```{r echo=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=2.5, message=F, warning=F}
articles |>
  mutate(res = statmod::qresid(m_art)) |>
  filter(ment < 60) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = ment, y = res)) +
  geom_point(size=0.5) +
  geom_smooth() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Number of articles published by mentor",
       y = "Quantile residuals")
```


## QQ plot

**If** the model is a good fit to the data, randomized quantile residuals should be approximately $N(0, 1)$.

```{r echo=F, message=F, warning=F, fig.height=3, fig.width=3}
articles |>
  mutate(res = statmod::qresid(m_art)) |>
  ggplot(aes(sample = res)) +
  geom_qq(size = 0.5) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, 
              lty = 2, color = "orange") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Theoretical normal quantiles",
       y = "Observed residual quantiles")
```

## A goodness-of-fit test

## A goodness-of-fit test

```{r}
m_art <- glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, 
             family = poisson, data = articles)

m_art$deviance
m_art$df.residual

pchisq(m_art$deviance, m_art$df.residual, lower.tail=F)
```

\vspace{3cm}

## A goodness-of-fit test

## Parametric bootstrapping

## Parametric bootstrapping

```{r par_boot, cache = T, include=F, message=F, warning=F}
m_art <- glm(art ~ phd + ment + kid5, 
             family = poisson, data = articles)

nsim <- 10000
n <- nrow(articles)
boot_dev <- rep(NA, nsim)
for(i in 1:nsim){
  articles_sim <- articles |>
    mutate(art_sim = rpois(n, m_art$fitted.values))
  m_sim <- glm(art_sim ~ phd + ment + kid5, 
             family = poisson, data = articles_sim)
  boot_dev[i] <- m_sim$deviance
}
```

```{r, echo=F, fig.width=4, fig.height=2.5, message=F, warning=F}
data.frame(boot_dev) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = boot_dev)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Deviance",
       title = "Parametric bootstrap distribution of deviance")
```

```{r}
m_art$deviance
```

## Approximate null distribution

**If** the model is a good fit to the data, then the residual deviance approximately follows a $\chi^2$ distribution, with the same degrees of freedom as the residual deviance.

```{r}
m_art$deviance
m_art$df.residual
```

\vspace{3cm}


## Summary so far

For the Poisson regression on the articles data, here is my perspective:

* There are several potential outliers
* The rootogram shows our predicted counts are somewhat low in the tails of the distribution, compared to the observed counts
* Quantile residual plots suggest the shape assumption is overall pretty reasonable
* The QQ plot suggests that variability of the residuals is higher than expected
* The goodness-of-fit test suggests that some part of our model is mis-specified

**Question:** If this particular model is mis-specified, what do you think is the cause? How could we modify the model?
